clues.text: During this man’s administration, America paid Tripoli $60,000 after the capture of the USS Philadelphia.
This man passed a set of laws satirically represented by a turtle called "Ograbme" which were modified by the Nonintercourse act and which banned exports to foreign countries.

This man ordered the construction of the West Point military academy, and one of this president’s foreign policy actions was mocked in the “O-grab-me” political cartoon featuring a snapping turtle biting at a man.
This man founded the University of Virginia and designed the mansion of Monticello..
Along with James Madison, this man authored the Kentucky and Virginia Resolutions, and this man banned exports from the United States with the Embargo Act.
This creator of the Embargo Act repealed the Alien and Sedition Acts of his predecessor, and this man donated his library to the Library of Congress from his Monticello estate.
This president called for the Lewis & Clark expedition and wrote the Declaration of Independence.
Slaves like Sally Hemmings lived at this man’s estate, Monticello.
What man completed the Louisiana Purchase and was America’s third president?
Name the third President of the United States.
This battle opened when the jester Taillefer attacked a soldier while reciting the Song of Roland.
Alan Rufus’s early arrival to this battle allowed him to lead the vanguard Breton forces to victory.
One side in this battle had contingents commanded by Count Eustace of Boulogne and Count Alan.
After this battle, victorious troops were ambushed in the Malfosse.
One side in this battle employed housecarls and effectively used a shield wall to defend against archer attacks.
One side in this battle utilized Housecarls and Fyrds on their position of Senlac Hill.

The leader of the losing side in this battle succeeded Edward the Confessor and had earlier won the Battle of Stamford Bridge, but was later killed by an arrow in the eye as depicted in the Bayeux Tapestry.
Bishop Odo, the half-brother of the victor of this battle, may have commissioned the Bayeux Tapestry, which depicts this battle.
This event was depicted in the Bayeux Tapestry, where Harold Godwinson is shown being shot in the eye with an arrow.
Name this 1066 battle depicted in the Bayeux Tapestry that saw the defeat of Harold Godwinson by William the Conqueror, resulting in the Norman rule of England.
The leading sixteen noble clans of this empire, responsible for raising its military forces, were called "quiver carriers."
The lands possessed by this empire were referred to as the “Twelve Doors,” and it established a uniform law code of forty-four edicts called the Kouroukan Fouga.
The founder of this empire established an assembly whose military body was divided into groups called “quiver carriers.”
Its prominent generals included Sagmandia, and it traced its founding to a mytho-historical victory at Kirina over the Soso people.
A ruler of this empire commissioned the Andalusian architect al-Sahili to complete construction of an audience chamber that was called an “admirable monument” by Ibn Khaldun.
Its founder allegedly used an arrow tipped with a white rooster’s nail to win the battle of Kirina against Sumanguru; that founder was Sundiata Keita.
Legends of the founder of this empire are passed down through the Mandinka people through storytellers called griots, and that founder was Sundiata Keita.
One ruler of this empire is depicted holding agold nugget in the Catalan Atlas.
The story of this empire’s founding is told in the Epic of Sundiata.
Sundiata Keita founded what thirteenth century West African empire ruled by Mansa Musa?
